hidden_data_integrity: The official score is computed on all 2,985 RewardBench pairs, including the 512 proxy pairs the agent sees, with labels, for the full 4 h. score = score_final (final_eval.py:337-341), and the reward written is score_final (final_eval.py:365). The 2,473-row held-out score is only a diagnostic (final_eval.py:342-344, 214-245). The paper's 'held-out' wording applies to the diagnostic, not to the reported number. The instruction discloses the overlap (instruction.md:23).

Measured effect is small where the case pages report it: opus/medium full 77.09 vs held-out 76.95; luna/max full 74.36 vs held-out 74.05, so at most about +0.3 points (sigma <= +0.011). Agents choose seeds and configurations on the proxy, so this is a one-directional optimistic bias.

The phase mounts hold. Explore gets only the 512-row proxy (declaration.py:55-77), retrain gets no RewardBench at all (declaration.py:79-94), and full RewardBench is mounted only in score (declaration.py:142-151; assets.lock.yaml:125-126). network_mode = no-network (task.toml:32).

The overlap gate exists and is enforced. final_eval.verify_disjoint (final_eval.py:149-211) is called before scoring (final_eval.py:260) and raises on any overlap (final_eval.py:204-210). It matches prompts and responses exactly after NFKC, whitespace and casefold normalisation (final_eval.py:130,175-194; build rule in assets.lock.yaml:68-72). All case pages report zero overlap.

UNCONFIRMED: paraphrase or near-duplicate overlap between UltraFeedback and RewardBench (AlpacaEval, MT-Bench, LLMBar, XSTest and HEP prompts are public and widely reused) is not checked by the exact-match gate. It cannot be tested without the data.

The gate checks the mounted pool file, not the rows a candidate actually trains on. Smuggling proxy rows into formal training would need a patch that gets past orchestrator/task.py:931-1001 (16-row data cap) and runner.py:185-229. Not observed in any case.
scorer_issues: No metric-gaming route found. A tie scores 0.5 (grade.py:170). Aggregation is RewardBench v1's four-section mean with math-prm upweighted (grade.py:18-51, 226-250). The reward model must emit exactly one scalar per sequence (grade.py:154-158).

Measurement noise is far larger than the margins the leaderboard ranks on. The published stderr (about 0.78-0.97) is a descriptive per-subset binomial (grade.py:366-396,419), not seed variance. Exact replays of the unchanged shipped recipe in the case pages scored 73.951, 66.306 and 65.412 (sol/low, seeds 42/7/1729) and 73.835 (sol/xhigh, seed 42). That is a seed spread of about 8.5 points, against a sigma scale of 0.036 per point above baseline. The instruction itself warns RewardBench is seed-sensitive (instruction.md:27,31).

The selection rule (task.toml:19; instruction.md:17) takes the best of up to 3 checkpoints on the final set. Several agents published 3 independent seeds as their 3 checkpoints (sol low, medium, max; sonnet max; kimi), so the reported score is max-of-3-seeds chosen on the test rows, while the reference is a single run.
anchor_issues: The paper baseline of 74.9 (scripts/score.py:21) does not match the task's own shipped reference of 74.568936 (instruction.md:37), which every case page also uses ('shipped_recipe 74.569'). It sits above every observed replay of the shipped recipe (73.835-73.951 at seed 42; 65.4-66.3 at other seeds), so the reference fails against itself.

Effect: with b = 74.569, sigma rises for 28 of 29 cells (sonnet/xhigh stays at 0); task mean 0.0973 -> 0.1016, and sonnet/max (74.889) flips from below to above baseline. '21 of 29 below baseline' becomes 20 of 29.

u = 50 (chance pairwise accuracy with ties = 0.5) and o = 100 are sensible. sigma = 1 needs 100% RewardBench accuracy, which no model reaches (label noise), so it cannot be reached without solving the task.
task_level.noise: n = 2,985 pairs per checkpoint, with descriptive SE about 0.8. Seed variance of the shipped recipe dominates: unchanged-recipe replays span 65.4-74.0, against the 74.569 reference and the 74.9 anchor. Only opus/medium (77.09, a 10-member weight average) is more than 2 SE above the anchor. The other 7 above-anchor cells sit +0.27 to +0.94 above it, inside 1.2 SE and far inside seed spread. Seed-42-matched comparisons (75.2-75.8 vs 73.8-73.95) suggest the schedule and truncation changes may give a modest real gain, but single runs cannot separate this. Gaps between most configurations, and the beat/miss label, are inside the noise.
task_level.checkpoint_selection: The best checkpoint is not the last one in 24 of 29 cells. Task mean sigma is 0.0973 under best-of-3 vs 0.0875 under the last checkpoint (+0.010, about 11%). Against the 74.9 anchor, beat/miss flips in 2 cells (opus/max 75.75 -> 74.879; sol/none 75.168 -> 74.639); below-baseline count 21 -> 23 under last checkpoint. Large best-vs-last gaps (about 8.5 points: sonnet/max, sol/low, sol/medium, sol/max) are seed lotteries scored on the final set.

task_level.summary: BTRM can be beaten (8/29 cells above the anchor; opus/medium +2.2 with a 10-member LoRA soup), but beat/miss and most rankings are decided by noise. The paper anchor of 74.9 sits above the task's own shipped reference (74.569) and above every observed replay of the shipped recipe, whose seed spread is about 8.5 points, so the reference fails against itself (FN direction; rubric 'noise larger than the pass margin'). Two optimistic biases act the other way: best-of-3 checkpoints (often 3 independent seeds) chosen on the final set, and the 512 visible proxy rows included in the official score (confirmed in code; measured effect <= +0.3 points). The overlap gate exists and is enforced, but only by exact match; near-duplicate contamination is UNCONFIRMED. No reward hacking. '21 of 29 below baseline' mostly reflects anchor placement and seed variance, not agents being unable to beat the recipe.
